title: Operation Sana: The 5th Corps Breaks South and East
content:
For three years, ARBiH 5th Corps defended the isolated Bihac pocket in northwestern Bosnia under pressure from VRS forces, the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and Fikret Abdic's APWB forces. BB2 pp. 536-538 provide the Bihac/APWB and ARBiH 5th Corps source trail for the formation whose later 1995 breakout is described here.

In September and October 1995, after Operation Storm and NATO's Operation Deliberate Force changed the western Bosnia military setting, 5th Corps advanced from the Bihac pocket toward Bosanski Petrovac, Kljuc, Bosanska Krupa, and Sanski Most. Bosanski Petrovac fell on 15 September, Ključ two days later, and Bosanska Krupa followed as the offensive widened. After VRS counterattacks around Sanski Most and Kljuc, Dudakovic renewed the assault on 9 October; Sanski Most fell on 10 October.

The immediate operational result was a major shift of the western Bosnia front before the October ceasefire. The 5th Corps advance moved RS-held territory eastward toward the territorial line that shaped the Dayton settlement, while Croatian and HVO operations pressed the VRS from other directions. This Codex entry keeps the claim bounded to actor, date window, direction, named places, and operational result.
